markdown: ## Watchlist - **Barclays:** It is stuck with UBS holding €1.2bn of debt after the Irca deal unravelled [Bloomberg.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiswFBVV95cUxNSndzbnQ5Mk41VWpmSzAzR1JoLW9QUWtwd0xUbDlfTHhLYm1lYlBnT1dRR2lkVGRMbkw4Q3JuTHdvR05MenlJUWZyQzF2N0dfMDNhSW9WR1FING1udHViaXJwWUlMWXZxMnRjajlHbTdnSlFUS056bm9XYUNveklDUGV2N1hSZmhtSmE0eWVCT1QyUWVHanhqc0duYzRubE5oZlNxX2NaTlc3MlNRalh2a1p4TQ?oc=5). Hung leveraged loans tie up balance sheet, so watch whether that affects Barclays' appetite for new corporate lending. - **UniCredit:** Italian bank consolidation is in focus amid Intesa's takeover bid for MPS and the UniCredit–Commerzbank merger [Il Sole 24 ORE](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiywFBVV95cUxNQ3g1WFRUTWRCUndxMG1zUnFITzJyT3phRk5rSkhlMDgwRHRhbGtxblJnMFg1T3d2NFJsRHNVT0F4VDZkQUFFcV9CRVNOQ0Nta2tOdm1FalhyXzhoNko5NWthOExsYzNHSS1uYTNGYTBVaFFFNXNfZ1ZLVlpkeTVSLTFjMHEzZ2JXMHMzY0VNd1RTQVA2UXV1Z0pWa0E5Y3k1S1dkaS02TmNNUG9sVGkyTzBsd2xhVC1hbktPVFROVnVxSHZZZVk0TWxNRQ?oc=5). Expect more consolidation, and fewer, bigger banking counterparties in Europe. - **JPMorgan:** It is working with Hyundai Card on AI agent transactions that don't involve humans [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/jpmorgan-hyundai-card-ai-agents-payments.html). This will become a controls question for corporates too. ## The brief - **Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, and the shares jumped more than 30%** [CFO Dive](https://www.cfodive.com/news/nvidia-reinstates-huang-as-chief-kress-remains-cfo-AI/875465/). The Nasdaq rose 7% and the S&P 500 4.7% [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/0f5a7285-fbf1-4120-86df-c9cca29644fc?syn-25a6b1a6=1). Strategists see this steadying the AI sell-off for now, but data-centre spending risks remain, so keep a cautious data-centre cooling assumption in the plan. - **The Fed's John Williams says higher interest rates are likely "over time" to address inflation** [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/john-williams-fed-inflation-rate-hikes.html). He expects inflation to get closer to 2% in 2027. Plan for USD floating costs to keep rising through next year. - **HVAC manufacturers reported higher revenue for Q3, and a study shows heat pump adoption surging in new construction** [ACHR News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilgFBVV95cUxQVzdLZ0JLZWJUakQ4Ym1vdFFUeFZBZ3dZdEQzRlNibkxLazBwMHdCU0V1ZGt1SE55OWc4aUJpR0hYcjFCMFJhczRrZklOUEljWHc5RjJCczZiQ2VPRkJqTFdYOS04UnFkdkdqWXJLT3BWUGRhRHd3MW9wdHZra2hfdmxrRDN4TU82NlhVZWJVRE9HU0hkcUE?oc=5)[ACHR News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilwFBVV95cUxNZGFkbkgzOHRUU25VbDNtbWJkUVpTbklnSlYwTEdfQWUxZUtBVTc0eWQtTXZ6dU5lMHNyN1h2UTl5b2NWeFBQcElLcm85clVjOG1kR0J5eHdQelhEcUNTRjQzYXBERmRwbkdGLS1Qbm91QWVYYkd2NjNTUU1vTDJKRExnb3g1RWlObmUwZVJQRXJYdkt0WUw4?oc=5). Demand is supportive, but higher volumes can tie up cash in receivables and inventory, so watch working capital. - **Recent stress in money markets is likely to push the Fed to expand its balance sheet before it moves to shrink it next year**, according to the FT [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/be4b5919-1d5a-4706-a942-800ccf157601). Funding conditions could stay choppy, so keep short-term liquidity buffers and CP backstops solid. ## Rates & FX - **The peso slide is accelerating.** USD/MXN rose 0.94% to 19.246, up 3.69% on the week. Mexican costs are now notably cheaper in dollars, so review whether to lock in more peso cost hedges. - **The dollar firmed again.** EUR/USD fell 0.46% to 1.0939 and GBP/USD fell 0.39% to 1.3074. USD/JPY is 159.07, USD/CNY eased to 6.6647 and EUR/GBP is 0.8367. - **Treasuries held Friday's rally.** The 2-year is 4.63% and the 10-year is 4.92%, both down 20bp on the week. SOFR is 3.92%, €STR is 2.444% and SONIA is 3.9841%. The ECB's Simkus says a December hike may not be enough, though he is in no rush to move again [Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuAFBVV95cUxQRFlkZVZKRk9QVlZVX0hUNXZSMWNqTG1oVXZ2cmw4V1VOMUMxV2NVS0djLTQ1M18wLXp6cE5iWkxSMzNwd0lyVHhETVNQY2Ffd25LVzQ1TUctV3E4YWRLZkNpSEhCZTJwMVBkc2RTZDgwSU9OX0lSOTFwY0xFd2hQVHdwVnhIeHhhWXJRZmtlNllyLUs3ZGJmakNCUTBGWGJ6Wk1za2IxMkIzZXhuUFk3eVIzQUpVVEFM?oc=5). - **No high-impact data today.** US core PCE (forecast +0.3%) and preliminary GDP (forecast 3.5% q/q) are due tomorrow at 13:30 Dublin. A hot PCE could undo the Treasury rally. ## Also worth knowing - **The ECB has expanded its acceptance of DLT-based assets as eligible Eurosystem collateral** [ECB](https://www.ecb.europa.eu//press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr261123~76b6f57b74.en.html). - **Morgan Stanley says European banks are set to fire up M&A talks** [Bloomberg.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxQN2RtZHR0VHlSQTlEem9rWFpIQi1qcTc1cUhYUHNOeW9HRlZ3X3VQMmhIUmh1Rkc2QXl5Z1VvbzhMSkxQcV9pbmUwZWNxR3ZuVVZ6WUcyelFSa3dvQVdqaFJqb1ZuakVaSGlPcHNJUEJTQlVGcWJiLVhPcEk0a19PQlFnSndhREJGRVBmclpXSGpRTlg3ZGF6Q05jU0dxdWVTd0ZoUFBpS0tiRVYwTXlV?oc=5). - **The US House is likely to pass a permitting bill with minimal changes, which industry groups say will make permitting much faster and cheaper for manufacturers** [Manufacturing Dive](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/house-passage-permitting-bill-likely-minimal-changes-nam/875349/). - **European fertiliser suppliers are shutting plants as energy prices soar, with a third of ammonia production suspended** [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/97e74bf5-081b-4f56-900f-36f1fd3b0e20?syn-25a6b1a6=1). ## Worth thinking about A Gartner survey finds CFOs are prioritising cost control and efficiency for 2027, as AI investment, persistent inflation and higher borrowing costs complicate the picture [CFO Dive](https://www.cfodive.com/news/cfos-prioritize-cost-control-efficiency-for-2027-ai-gartner/875536/). For treasury, a good question is which costs we control directly, such as bank fees, FX spreads and idle cash, and whether a structured review could fund part of the efficiency target.
